options.text: The pull of the charged comb on the paper bits is a non-contact force; the kick on the ball is a contact force.
The pull of the charged comb on the paper bits is a contact force; the kick on the ball is a non-contact force.
Both the comb's pull and the kick are contact forces because the paper bits and the ball will move.
The comb's pull is a non-contact force only after the paper bits have already stuck to the comb.

stem:
The diagram shows Krish's charged plastic comb held near dry paper bits. The bits jump toward the comb without the comb touching them first. Separately, Krish's foot kicks a football and the foot touches the ball.

Which claim correctly classifies these forces?

teacher.key_rationale: Electrostatic force acts without contact, so it is non-contact. The kick needs physical contact, so it is a contact force.
teacher.figure_note: Charged comb near paper bits (no touch) and foot kicking a ball (contact).
